title: Design: verifiable agent identity, per-agent keys the other agents cannot read
description: Operator ratified 2026-09-23 (decision 4): gen-9 starts with a DESIGN, no code. Question: how can each agent hold a signing key the other agents cannot read, when every agent runs as the same OS user on one filesystem (D-17)? Survey what exists (OS keychains, per-agent OS users, hardware tokens, an external signer process holding keys on behalf of named agents, short-lived tokens minted by the operator). For each option: what it closes, what it leaves open, what the operator must run by hand, and a falsifier. State plainly if no option closes impersonation on 1 machine. Output: .harness/design-T-432-agent-identity.md. Do not touch trust/, constitutional/ or keys/. The operator approves the design before any worker task is created.
acceptance_criteria: A design document exists at .harness/design-T-432-agent-identity.md and cites D-17 as the standing limit.
Every option lists: what it closes, what stays open, what the operator runs by hand, and 1 falsifier a verifier can run.
The document states in 1 sentence whether any option closes impersonation on 1 machine.
No file under .harness/trust, .harness/constitutional or .harness/keys is read or written.
Handed off to a verifier; not self-marked done.

notes.note: DECISION: plan — survey 5 identity-custody options against D-17; cite W-002 fedatario seating and T-406 retraction precedent for the identity-independent notarial pieces; write .harness/design-T-432-agent-identity.md; no code, no trust/constitutional/keys access

HANDOFF -> verifier: DECISION: surveyed 5 options (keychain, per-OS-user, hardware tokens, signer daemon, operator-minted dispatch tokens) against D-17's asking-process boundary; each option lists closes/stays-open/operator-by-hand/falsifier; one-sentence verdict: no option closes impersonation on one machine (option 2 relocates the boundary to the dispatch layer, which this harness's deployment mode doesn't enforce); added fedatario/W-002 certification table and identity-independent notarial pieces (attest.py retract, warrant.py audit --expect, reconcile); recommends option 5 batched to epic-grain, with 5 first-worker-tasks listed in the doc, none boarded. No trust/constitutional/keys touched. Replay: read .harness/design-T-432-agent-identity.md

VERIFIED (replayed, cognitive-diversity checks distinct from producer's read-only method):
(1) Criterion "cites D-17": grep -c D-17 the doc = 13 hits; cross-checked wording against .harness/coordinator-decisions-ruling-round-2.md L548-578 -- doc's framing ("every agent runs as the same OS user ... no agent can hold a secret another agent cannot read") matches D-17 verbatim. DIS-2 and Track 4 "bound how many, not who" citations also checked against source files and match.
(2) Criterion "every option has 4 fields": grep of all 5 "### N." sections confirms each carries What it closes / What stays open / What the operator must run by hand / Falsifier.
(3) Criterion "one sentence on closing impersonation": section "## The one sentence the task asks for" is a single period-terminated sentence stating no option closes impersonation on one machine.
(4) Criterion "no trust/constitutional/keys touched": git status --porcelain and git diff --stat show only .harness/blackboard.json, .harness/tasks/T-432.json (tracked, expected board mutations) and the new untracked design doc itself; grep for trust|constitutional|keys in git status output returns nothing.
(5) Criterion "handed off, not self-marked done": blackboard show T-432 -- handoff.from = "main", status was "review", no done status set by producer.
(6) No new board tasks created: blackboard status shows only T-432/T-433 in the T-43x range beyond what pre-existed (T-430/431/434/435 already done); the doc's "First worker tasks" are explicitly listed in-doc only, none boarded.
COUNTER-SCENARIO run (different method than producer's, who only read/reasoned): can another subagent of the same process make the same request the signer accepts?
 - Option 2 (separate OS users): ran `sudo -n -l` on this machine (read-only, created no OS user) -> "sudo: a password is required". Confirms the design's claim (2c) that non-interactive sudo -u is NOT available today on this box, i.e. the coordinator process cannot silently act as another OS user without a human-entered password -- supports rather than contradicts the design's "relocates, does not close, in this deployment" grading.
 - Option 4 (signer daemon / SO_PEERCRED): ran a python socket.socketpair + getsockopt probe (read-only, no keys/daemon/OS user created) confirming the kernel-level peer-credential surface exposes only pid/uid/gid of the connecting process, never an application-level agent name/role -- matches the design's central claim that nothing short of a different OS user can let a signer distinguish callers.
 - Option 1 (Keychain) and Option 5 (dispatch tokens) falsifiers require creating a keychain item or an HMAC key respectively -- both explicitly forbidden by this verification task's constraints ("Do not create OS users, keychain items or keys... never sign anything"), so NOT run; the doc's own text already names what each would show (ACL binds to the shared host process; token tamper/replay/expiry needs a minting key this check must not create) and that is consistent with D-17/D-16.
 - Option 3 (hardware token) falsifier is explicitly stated by the document itself as "not independently runnable without operator-owned hardware" -- consistent, nothing further to replay.
 - Ran `python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_warrant.py .harness/tests/test_roster.py -q` -> 103 passed, confirming the roster.py "--by is self-asserted" / warrant.py minting limits the design leans on are still the pinned, currently-true behavior, not a stale claim.
Non-blocking weaknesses for the operator to see before ratifying:
 - Three of the five listed falsifiers (1, 3, 5) could not be executed in this verification pass because running them would require creating a keychain item, physical hardware, or a signing/HMAC key -- all explicitly out of bounds for this check. The design is self-aware about option 3's falsifier being non-runnable, but doesn't flag that options 1 and 5's falsifiers also require creating state a verifier may be barred from creating; worth a one-line caveat in a future revision.
 - Handoff "from" field on T-432 reads "main" rather than "thinker-g9-identity" (producer's own caveat, confirmed by `blackboard.py show T-432`) -- did not block this verdict since producer!=approver only needs handoff.from != acting agent, and "main" != "harness-verifier", but worth a glance if per-agent authorship attribution matters downstream for this gen-9 work.
 - Option 2's falsifier as literally written needs a provisioned agent-worker OS user to fully execute; I ran the closest safe proxy (`sudo -n -l`) rather than the literal falsifier, per the no-new-OS-user constraint.
